title: Streaming prefill preprocessor and per-customer prefix cache to cut prefill-side overhead
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: For high-throughput hosted traffic, prefill-side overhead (prompt tokenization + prefix processing) is a measurable fraction of end-to-end latency and CPU cost. Current flow does full tokenization and prefix concatenation per request before handing off to the GPU serving path. This becomes costly for short prompts, high-concurrency customers, and when many requests share identical instruction/system prefixes.

Goal: Reduce per-request prefill overhead by introducing a streaming tokenizer path that begins producing encoded token chunks to the serving runtime immediately, and a per-customer immutable prefix cache that stores tokenized system/instruction prefixes (including KV prefill metadata) to avoid redundant work. The solution should preserve correctness for edge cases (dynamic prompt templates, user-specific interpolation) and be safe for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Outcomes we want: 20-40% reduction in median prefill CPU time for 90th percentile of traffic, 10-25% improvement in end-to-end median latency for short prompts (<=32 tokens), and reduction in tokenization-related cost for customers with high reuse of prefixes.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming prefill path implemented and gated behind feature flag: runtime accepts partial token chunks and proceeds with KV prefill as soon as the prefix is available.
Per-customer prefix cache implemented with size/eviction policy configurable from Console; cache keys include model, quantization variant, prefix-hash, and tenant-id.
Benchmarks show >=20% CPU-time reduction on synthetic short-prompt workload and >=10% median latency improvement in canary region vs baseline.
E2E tests cover dynamic interpolation, per-request overrides (force-recompute), and cache invalidation on prefix change.
Design doc and Confluence spec approved by runtime and infra leads (security review if KMS is referenced).
Rollout plan with canary, metrics (prefill_cpu_ms, prefill_wall_ms, total_latency_ms), and automatic rollback conditions defined in Console rollout config.
technical_notes: Streaming tokenizer: wrap existing tokenizer into an async iterator that yields token-id chunks (256 token chunks max) and byte-offset metadata; runtime will accept first N tokens to warm KV cache while continuing to receive rest.
Prefix cache key: sha256(tenant_id + model_spec + prefix_source_hash + kernel_signature). Storing both token-ids and serialized KV cache snapshots (when available) to accelerate cold-starts.
Memory/eviction: default max entries per-tenant 1k with LRU; global memory cap 12GB for hosted API. Cache entries are reference-counted to prevent eviction during ongoing prefill operations.

Correctness: if prefix contains request-time interpolations (e.g., {{user.name}}) we mark as non-cacheable unless template fully resolved before tokenization. Provide opt-in API for 'cacheable_prefix' boolean at request time.

Interaction with kernel selection & attention optimizations: streaming prefill can reveal sequence-length distribution earlier to the kernel selector, enabling earlier selection of fused attention kernels appropriate for short sequences. Need to update kernel-selection heuristics to accept partial-length hints and re-evaluate if final length crosses thresholds.
Compatibility: path must be available for hosted and Dedicated. Private deployments may disable shared prefix cache; provide a local-only cache mode and clear guidance for on-prem sizing.

Security: cached payloads are plaintext token ids and small KV snapshots; ensure tenant isolation and optional encryption-at-rest for Private tier. Mark for security_review_required in sensitive deployments.
Telemetry: new metrics: prefill_streaming_enabled (bool), prefill_cache_hit_ratio, prefill_serialize_ms, prefill_first_kv_ready_ms. Add tracing spans around tokenizer and cache lookup.

Open trade-offs: (1) Caching KV snapshots speeds warmups but increases memory and complexity with kernel/quantization mismatches; (2) Streaming increases concurrency and backpressure complexity on runtime input queues. Initial implementation will cache only token sequences + small KV hints (seq_len, special_tokens) and defer full KV snapshot caching to a later iteration.
Related PR: runtime change for accept-partial-prefill - https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321 (WIP). Tokenizer refactor PR - https://github.com/redwood-inference/tokenizers/pull/88.
Benchmark harness: created a synthetic harness in infra-perf repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-perf/tree/main/prefill_streaming_bench. Baseline run (2026-02-28) attached in links.
implementation_plan: Spike (2d): implement async iterator tokenizer shim and microbenchmark token chunk latency; verify no change in token ids across streams.
Prototype (4d): implement in-hosted runtime accept-first-chunk path, integrate with simple in-memory prefix cache; feature-flagged.
Canary (3d): deploy to canary region for 2 customers with high prefix reuse; collect metrics and adjust eviction/prefetch thresholds.
Iterate (5d): add kernel-selector hints integration and safety checks for quantization/kernel mismatches; implement eviction/refcount logic.
GA (2d): enable default for hosted API, add Console controls, document sizing for Dedicated/Private and provide migration guide.
Follow-ups: full KV snapshot caching, Console telemetry dashboards, and automatic cache warming based on traffic patterns.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded. We agreed to prioritize short-prompt improvement for chat-style workloads. Action: Diego to spike streaming tokenizer.

2026-03-01 - Diego Morales: Spike complete. Async tokenizer yields first token chunk in ~1.2ms vs 4.8ms for full tokenization on a long prompt. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tokenizers/pull/88. Observed minor differences in special token handling — fixed in tokenizer shim.
2026-03-04 - Priya Anand (PM): Reviewed prototype. Asking for explicit API flag to opt-out of caching for enterprises concerned about data residency. Also requested Console toggle for cache sizing.
2026-03-06 - Security review request filed to SecOps: need guidance on encryption-at-rest and per-tenant isolation for cached KV hints.

2026-03-09 - Diego Morales: Canary deploy in us-west-2 running. Initial telemetry: prefill_cache_hit_ratio ~0.48 for one test tenant, median prefill_cpu_ms down 30% on test waveform. Observed increased memory pressure, raised global cap and implemented refcounting to avoid mid-prefill eviction.

2026-03-11 - Ming Zhao (Runtime Lead): Reviewed kernel-selector integration. Suggested adding re-evaluation window when final sequence length > streaming_hint + 32 tokens to prevent inefficient kernel choice for long tails.

2026-03-12 - Diego Morales: Updated implementation to include re-eval hook and added unit tests covering cache invalidation when prefix hash changes. Preparing PR for runtime: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321.
Next steps: complete security review, finalize Console settings UX with Design, and schedule Dedicated sizing guidance writeup.
